title: Tenant-windowed decelerator and KV heatmap allocator to smooth microburst backpressure
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem:
High-QPS tenant bursts cause transient microbursts that fill GPU KV cache and trigger excessive microbatching/backpressure oscillation. This creates tail-latency spikes and uneven fairness across tenants. Existing admission heuristics react to slot/gpu headroom metrics but do not incorporate tenant-level burst pacing nor the evolving key hotness distribution.

Hypothesis:
Bounding microburst admission using a tenant-windowed deceleration factor plus a KV heatmap-driven allocator will: (1) smooth short-term QPS spikes into steadier request arrival patterns, (2) proactively spill or deprioritize low-value KV entries when a tenant's heatmap indicates superlinear hot-key growth, and (3) reduce 95/99th token-latency under sustained high QPS without materially reducing throughput for steady tenants.

Design (high level):
- Tenant-windowed decelerator: maintain a short rolling window per tenant (configurable: 500ms/1s/2s) that tracks request arrival rate and assigns a deceleration factor d in (0,1] used by the admission controller to probabilistically delay or admit requests into the next microbatch. Deceleration is a continuous multiplier (not hard throttle) to avoid synchronization effects.
- KV heatmap allocator: lightweight per-tenant key-frequency heatmap (approx-count sketch) exported to the admission layer. If hot-key density crosses thresholds, allocator signals: preemptive spill candidate list, reduced cache residency score for cold shards, and increased chance of short delay via decelerator.
- GPU-memory estimator: integrate heatmap and model token-state footprint to predict near-term KV memory delta; admission controller integrates predicted delta into headroom scoring to avoid sudden OOM/eviction cascades.
- Policies: tiered profiles (prod, burst-friendly, best-effort) exposed in config. Canary rollout flags for progressive enablement per fleet.
- Telemetry: per-tenant deceleration factor, heatmap entropy, predicted KV delta, actual KV evictions, microbatch size distribution, per-model tail token latency.

API/Config changes:
- admission.config.tenant_window_ms (int)
- admission.config.deceleration_curve (enum: linear, exponential, sigmoid)
- kv.heatmap.sketch_size (int)
- rollout flags: feature.decelerator, feature.kv_heatmap_allocator

Experiment plan:
1) Unit tests for decelerator math and stochastic admission.
2) Local sim harness (Replay service) using production traces with injected bursts (x2-x10 spike profiles).
3) Perf tests on staging fleet (10 GPU nodes) with mixed tenants. Measure 95/99 token latencies, KV residency, eviction counts, throughput, and fairness index.
4) Small canary (5% prod traffic) -> monitor for unintended tail regressions.

Rollout and safety:
- Default to off. Enable per-customer via feature flag. Ramp to 25%/50%/100% after SLO checks.
- Fallback: if predicted KV delta > X or observed evictions spike > Y in 1m, automatically disable decelerator for affected tenant and fall back to legacy admission.

Rationale for novelty:
Existing tickets focused heavily on global microbatch thresholds and reservoir controllers. This work adds tenant-windowed pacing and a compact heatmap to inform admission decisions at tenant granularity while preserving continuous batching benefits. It is designed to avoid global oscillation by making deceleration probabilistic and time-bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic burst test: under 8x injected QPS spikes, 95th token latency improves >= 40% compared to baseline for affected tenants (measured over 10m windows)
KV stability: average per-tenant KV evictions per minute does not increase > 15% for steady tenants in mixed workload tests
Fairness: measured fairness index (Jain) across tenants improves or stays within 5% of baseline for steady tenants
No regressions: rollout to 5% canary shows no SLO regressions on production dashboards for > 30m; automated rollback triggers function as specified
Telemetry: deceleration factor, heatmap entropy, predicted KV delta, and eviction signals are emitted and visible in console dashboards

2026-03-03 Jonas Meyer (review): Reviewed math for deceleration curve. Concern: exponential curve may over-penalize short bursts. Suggested adding minimum admit probability to avoid starving small requests.
